title: lore check enforces validate's error-tier quote-safety findings, so the two gates cannot disagree (ADR-0007; LCLI-606 carve-out)
description: opum-agent ratified LCLI-606 (R11) as shipped on 2026-09-26T23:39:51Z, on one condition: the quote-safety carve-out must be explained, and filed as a follow-up if it means check and validate can disagree on the same file. They can. lore validate reports error-severity quote-safety findings on AUTHOR-WRITTEN frontmatter scalars that YAML-1.1 consumers read differently (src/core/validate.ts, "frontmatter quote-safety": a bare YYYY-MM-DD date, a bare yes/no/on/off, and YAML indicator characters), while lore check deliberately does not keep them (src/commands/check.ts validateRuleCheckFindings: "Not kept: quote-safety ..."). So a document with an unquoted date can exit 6 under validate and 0 under check: the defect ADR-0007 exists to prevent. Before changing it, measure the fleet by ref (as for LCLI-606 AC2) for error-tier quote-safety findings, since unlike R11 this may have real impact; route any hits to their owners, and treat it as a behaviour change with a CHANGELOG entry.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A fleet measurement by ref of error-tier quote-safety findings (repos read, files read, hits, positive control) is recorded here before the change lands, and any hit is routed to its owner
lore check reports every error-tier quote-safety finding lore validate reports, under the quote-safety rule name, proven by tests that assert the two gates agree on the same file
CHANGELOG marks it a behaviour change naming lore validate as the preview; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: AC1 FLEET MEASUREMENT 2026-09-28 ~16:50Z, by ref. Method (LCLI-606 AC2, adapted): each repo's origin/dev was fetched, exported with git archive into scratch, then git init + git add (no commit). lore validate --json ran from lore-cli source at origin/dev e7f20324. The count is findings with rule quote-safety and severity error; warnings were counted separately. REPOS READ: 11 of 11 with parseable JSON: opum-agent 3d4f9feb (17 files), opum-doc f7b549bf (183), lore-cli e7f20324 (82), quest-cli 8342cac9 (63), opum-cli-e2e 4e019125 (7), lore-web a14d6dd0 (13), quest-web 85a0abb4 (14), opum-web 809883cc (4), opum-marketplace 86aee66a (6), opum-fleet a10d004f (6), ward-cli 8b34a314 (1). That is 396 files, and every validate run exited 0. RESULT: 0 error-tier quote-safety findings in every repo, and 0 warning-tier findings too. Nothing needs routing to an owner. POSITIVE CONTROL, same pass: two lines were added to the frontmatter of opum-doc docs/adr/add-a-computed-dotted-display-id-over-quests-flat-canonical-sequence.md, in the export copy only: 'reviewed: 2026-09-28' and 'archived: yes'. validate then exited 6 with an ERROR for the bare yes and only a WARNING for the bare date. lore check on the same modified file exited 0, which reproduces the ADR-0007 disagreement this task exists to remove. The file was restored byte-identical (cmp), and validate re-read 0 errors. CORRECTION to this task's description: a bare YYYY-MM-DD date is WARNING-tier in validate, not error-tier, so only the bare boolean (and the indicator-character cases, per src/core/validate.ts) is in AC2's scope, since AC2 enforces error-tier only.
